messages.subject: Direct Labels Needs Color Aesthetic
parts:
Hello, 

So this is a directlabels problem, but its applied to ggplot2 so I hope its all fine to post it here. 

Using the data set attached. 

library(ggplot2)
library(directlabels)
d<-read.csv(file.choose(),header=T)   

I use the following setup:

> plot1 <- qplot ( TREAT, RAND, data = d, stat="summary", fun.y = "mean" , width = 1.5 , group = MALE, color = MALE) 

and then with directlabels:

> p1 <- direct.label (plot1, list ( "last.qp" , hjust = -1 , vjust = 0 , cex = 1 , rot = 20 ))  

I get a nice graph with the labels exactly where I want, but when I try to make all the lines black, by removing the 'color=MALE' direct labels returns an error: 

> plot1 <- qplot ( TREAT, RAND, data = d, stat="summary", fun.y = "mean" , width = 1.5 , group = MALE) 

> p1 <- direct.label (plot1, list ( "last.qp" , hjust = -1 , vjust = 0 , cex = 1 , rot = 20 )) 

This error returns:

> Error in direct.label.ggplot(plot1, list("last.qp", hjust = -1, vjust = 0,  : 
>   Need colour aesthetic to infer default direct labels.

I don't know how to work around this, or where I can use a alternative color aesthetic so that I don't get this error. 

All I need is for all the dots to be black, with the labels (in black also). 

Thanks,  

Ackley

messages.subject: Re: Direct Labels Needs Color Aesthetic
parts:
Hi Ackley,

You can set all the colors to be black using scale_color_manual(),
though I don't understand how you know how you are supposed to know
which group the TREAT=A points are in...

plot1 <- qplot (TREAT, RAND,

color = MALE) +
scale_colour_manual(values = rep("black", length(unique(d$MALE))))
